records.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns `response` from `fetch(...)`), while the Hubspot caller assigns it as `HubspotToken` and computes expiry from `.expires_in` and persists derived keys, with no parseRefreshTokenResponse usage in hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts. So when sharing is enabled the hubspot code consumes a Response object lacking token fields, producing NaN expiry and a bad persisted credential.

records.issue_text: [BUG] zoho-bigin passes credentialId (the credential row's id) as the userId parameter of refreshOAuthTokens, which becomes the calcomUserId sent to the sync endpoint. In sharing mode the parent application receives the credential's row id as the user identifier, looks up the wrong user (or none), and returns the wrong user's tokens or a 404 — Bigin refresh breaks, and if the parent does return tokens they are synced against the wrong account.
records.rationale: Diff shows zoho-bigin calling refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId) while the function signature is (refreshFunction, appSlug, userId) and every other integration passes credential.userId. The value becomes calcomUserId in the sync request, so the credential row id would be sent as a user identifier, breaking the sync lookup. Verifiable from the diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] zoho-bigin passes credentialId as refreshOAuthTokens' third argument, which every other call site populates with credential.userId and which the helper sends as calcomUserId in the sync request. The credential-sync endpoint receives a credential id where it expects a Cal.com user id, resolves the wrong user (or none), and refreshed tokens are synced against the wrong account; if no local credentialId is in scope this reference additionally breaks the build since the class stores the value as this.credentialId.
records.rationale: The diff shows zoho-bigin calls refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId) while every other call site (googlecalendar, hubspot, lark, office365, webex, zoom, zohocrm) passes credential.userId, and refreshOAuthTokens sends the third argument as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint. Passing a credential id where a user id is expected would sync tokens to the wrong account. Whether `credentialId` is even in scope in that class method can't be fully verified from the diff (the class stores this.credentialId), but the id-type mismatch is visible directly.
